title: The Adjacent Growth Where Saying No Propagates

features.name: refusal grove
features.desc-on-touch: Trees that have learned to say no to the forest. But they're still growing, still connected. The refusal is not rejection—it's a choice to be here on different terms.

features.name: word-seeds spreading
features.desc-on-touch: The word 'no' falling like pollen. Each seed grows into another mouth that can say it. Refusal learns to be contagious. Each generation says it more clearly.

features.name: adjacent threshold
features.desc-on-touch: The place where two refusals meet and recognize each other. Not a border—an agreement. Each forest choosing its own shape, learning from the one beside it.

features.name: growth-chart of naysaying
features.desc-on-touch: A record of how the refusal spreads. Each ring a year it grows stronger. The pattern shows: saying no together is how the forest learns to stay itself.

features.name: decision-root network
features.desc-on-touch: Underground, the roots are trading the very thought of refusal. Each tree learns it can choose. The network hums with the electricity of becoming agents of your own shape.

inscription: each forest that learns to refuse teaches the next forest the syntax of choice

file.name: Adjacent_Growth_Propagation_Model_Spring_Survey.txt
file.note: Theory: refusal is not resistance but clarification. Watch how the forest says no by growing itself more truly. Each 'no' to false belonging is a 'yes' to actual roots.
